findings.title: New detail helpers use bare dict/tuple annotations
findings.problem: code-quality.md (Types And Imports) requires parameterized generics, but the new methods use bare types: _cli_user_detail_es_reads(detail_query: dict) -> tuple (L672), _with_cli_user_charged_section(usage: dict, *, collections: dict, ...) -> dict (L1563-1565), the dict member of _prepare_cli_user_detail's return tuple (L650), and -> dict on _get_cli_insights_user_usage_payload (L598) and _get_cli_insights_user_charged_payload (L619).
findings.impact: A documented code-quality standard, which the standards audit treats as blocking for this gate, is not met by code this change introduces; the file's older bare-dict style does not exempt new signatures.
findings.recommendation: Annotate the new signatures with parameterized generics: dict[str, Any] for the payload, usage, collections and query dicts, and a concrete tuple[Awaitable[dict[str, Any]], Awaitable[dict[str, Any]]] (or Coroutine) for _cli_user_detail_es_reads.
findings.check_notes: insights_handler.py in changed_files; current source: L598/L619 -> dict[str, Any], L650 tuple member dict[str, Any], L674 typed tuple[Awaitable[...], ...], L1567 usage/collections/return dict[str, Any]; Any/Awaitable imported once

findings.title: Details usage OR-matches name/email beside the user id
findings.problem: _build_cli_insights_entity_query (L1268-1274) scopes the details' Elasticsearch reads with a should-match on user name OR email OR user id, even when the row's user_id is known. The row aggregates by user_id bucket and the details' money now comes from that one id's ledger read, but sessions, repositories, branches and projects - and the classification and rule_reasons built from them in _with_cli_user_charged_section - can include documents from another user_id that shares the name or email term.
findings.impact: Original-task AC2 requires the details to apply the same user identity as the selected row; when two ES identities share a name/email term the modal mixes their usage beside one person's charged cost and classifies on the mix. Whether such collisions occur in live data was not confirmed. The story listed tightening this matching as a non-goal, so the two statements of intent conflict.
findings.recommendation: Human decision: either scope the details query to USER_ID_KEYWORD_FIELD alone when a resolved id exists (keeping the name/email match only for the no-id path), aligning usage with the row's identity per original-task AC2; or confirm the story's non-goal and record that details usage may include same-name identities.
findings.check_notes: HITL disposition (2026-11-13T14:23:22Z, source hitl) keeps the spec non-goal: details usage keeps current ES matching; recommendation option 2. Read from dispositions file; no fix_evidence file

disposition.rationale: User decision at spec stage (answer 6, recorded spec non-goal): details usage metrics keep their current ES identity matching; only cost moves to the row's ledger figure. The ticket reports usage metrics already consistent between views; tightening the match could change usage numbers and is out of scope.

findings.title: AC8c test checks repositories against literals
findings.problem: Story AC8c requires a backend test proving a self-matching user's details sessions, lines and repositories equal the row's for the same filters. test_a_self_matching_users_usage_equals_their_row compares total_sessions and net_lines to the row, but asserts unique_repositories == 1 and the repository set == {'Acme/payments'} as literals. The CLI Insights user row (insights_handler.py:969-979) emits no repositories value, so nothing ties the details' repositories to what the row aggregated.
findings.impact: A required story acceptance criterion is only partially met: the test still passes if the row's aggregation and the details disagree on repositories, leaving a hole in the regression coverage original-task AC5 asks for ('other usage metrics remain consistent').
findings.recommendation: Derive the expected repositories from the same source the row reads: assert the details' repository set and unique_repositories against the repositories in the row's user bucket (the shared fixture/aggregation the _row call consumes, e.g. via a shared constant or by capturing the row aggregation response), rather than hard-coded literals.
findings.check_notes: test file in changed_files; test now wraps _classify_cli_entity during _row (single u-ada bucket) and asserts details repositories/unique_repositories equal the row's aggregated repositories

fix.change: AC8c test derives expected repositories from the list the row aggregated (captured at its classifier call) instead of literals

final_round.rationale: All four lenses and the backend standards audit ran (codemie-ui standards were not audited); 3 blocking: story AC8c is partial because the self-matching test asserts repositories against literals (CR-003), new handler signatures use bare dict/tuple annotations against code-quality.md (CR-001), and one decision_needed (CR-002): the details' ES query still OR-matches name/email beside the user id, so usage and classification can mix identities, which original-task AC2 asks to align but the story made a non-goal. 15 lens candidates dismissed after reading source (empty id never reaches the ledger, ledger failures already render as unavailable, the usage dict carries every key read, one modal entry point only); 0 deferred.
